nodes.name: Upload voiceover
nodes.notes: File upload exception: the published Zvid node does not expose multipart uploads. The upload step uses HTTP Request → `POST /api/uploads`, authenticated with the same **Zvid API** credential. All supported Zvid operations use the Zvid node.

parameters.content:
## Turn a blog post into a video

### How it works
Read your RSS feed, find a new post, and fetch the article text. Generate narration and stock footage, then render a captioned vertical summary. The feed excerpt is a fallback when the article cannot be fetched.

### Setup
1. Install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`** from **Settings → Community nodes** before credentials. A workspace owner/admin may need to install it.
2. Create a **Zvid API** credential with [your API key](https://app.zvid.io/api-keys) and Base URL `https://api.zvid.io`. Select it on every Zvid node and upload step.
3. Set feedUrl, brandName, colors and ctaText in Config.
4. Connect OpenRouter to Write script and ElevenLabs Header Auth (xi-api-key) to Generate voiceover.
5. **dryRun=false** renders and spends Zvid credits. Set it to **true** for an editor draft and quote. AI or transcription charges may still apply.
6. Test manually and review the output before activating automatic runs.

### Customization
Adjust branding, media and timing in the configuration node. Multipart upload uses HTTP Request because the published Zvid node lacks that operation. [Detailed setup guide](https://github.com/Zvid-io/zvid-n8n/blob/master/workflows/blog-to-video.md).

nodes.name: 1. Choose settings and an entry point

parameters.content:
## 1. Choose settings and an entry point

Complete the overview setup first. Use the manual trigger for a test, then check the trigger settings and workflow timezone before activation.

## 2. Find a new article

Read the configured RSS feed and skip posts already completed in production. An empty or inaccessible feed needs attention.

## 3. Read the article

Fetch the full page when available. The prompt falls back to feed text and should not invent missing facts.

## 4. Write and check the script

Generate concise copy from the supplied source. Review names, claims and attribution before sharing the finished video.

## 5. Choose footage for each scene

Search Zvid’s stock library and match footage to each scene. Review selected clips for relevance and attribution.

## 6. Check the background music

Check the configured track or stock candidates before use. Follow the guard’s result when music is unavailable.

## 7. Create narration and timings

Generate voice audio and caption timings. Multipart audio upload uses HTTP Request because the published Zvid node does not expose uploads.

## 8. Build and validate the design

Prepare the media and video design, then validate the payload and credit quote. Resolve validation errors before submitting a render.

## 9. Choose an optional editor preview

dryRun=true returns an editor draft and credit quote. The default false branch renders and spends Zvid credits; upstream AI services may charge separately.

## 10. Render and wait for completion

Submit the render, then check its status until completion or timeout. Keep each result paired with its source item. Check Zvid before retrying a timed-out job.

## 11. Review the finished media

Open Watch video → Binary → data → View. Select each output item for batches; image outputs open as images. Empty links and preview results skip the download.
